name: Equally Liked Nature, City and Animals: Image Ratings and Mood
description: Faithful replication of Study 4 in Meidenbauer, Stenfors, Bratman, Gross, Schertz, Choe & Berman (2020), "The affective benefits of nature exposure: What's nature got to do with it?", Journal of Environmental Psychology 72: 101498. Does nature improve mood more than other pictures people like just as much? Each participant is randomly assigned to one of three sets of 30 very highly liked photographs: natural scenes, city scenes or animals, matched on preference in the authors' validation study (Study 3). Mood is measured before and after viewing with the 6-item STAI (calm, relaxed, content; upset, tense, worried; 1–4) and four 1–100 visual analogue scales (happy, sad, inspired, angry). Each photograph stays on screen for at least 7 s and is then rated from 1 (strongly dislike) to 7 (strongly like). Answers use the same condition codes (Nat / Urb / Anim) and image names as the authors' open data on OSF (ehtk9), so results can be compared with Study4_data.csv. Photographs: the authors' Study 3 image sets from OSF ehtk9 (taken from the SUN database and non-copyrighted web images), used with credit to the authors; the template will be removed if the authors object. Differences from the original study: (1) the mood induction is left out: the original randomly assigned each participant to read a negative story or a neutral story (an excerpt from A Brief History of Time) for at least 2 minutes before the first mood measure; this template starts directly with the mood questions, which is closest to the neutral condition; (2) age and gender are asked on the first page; the original collected them as well but the position is not reported; (3) the order of the STAI items and of the four sliders is randomised on each page, which the paper does not specify.
author: Meidenbauer, Stenfors, Bratman, Gross, Schertz, Choe & Berman

elements.name: stai_t1
elements.title: Before the pictures (T1): how do you feel right now, at this moment?
elements.description: 6-item STAI (Marteau & Bekker, 1992), 1 = not at all … 4 = very much; item order random. STAI-Pos = mean(calm, relaxed, content), STAI-Neg = mean(upset, tense, worried), as STAI1_pos / STAI1_neg in the open data.

elements.title: How much do you like this image?
